newsitem.title: USA: Outright U.S. cash crudes retreat, grades steady.
newsitem.headline: Outright U.S. cash crudes retreat, grades steady.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gave back more than half of Wednesday's gains on the outright market, slipping lower on long liquidation ahead of August NYMEX products expiry.
Benchmark September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing lost 55 cents to $19.70-80 a barrel, and moved some 7-9 cents weaker than the second month October WTI/Cushing.

The wide swing in outrights resulted in a September Postings Plus values drop from more than $2.00 to around $1.90, traders in the U.S. Gulf said. A deal was actually heard at $2.04 very early Thursday, another source said.
The only other grade trade noted Thursday was a West Texas Sour/Midland parcel at a steady $1.38 discount to September WTI/Cushing.

Talk in the market concerns reports U.S. trader Bayoil is hunting for Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) to take Iraqi crude oil from the port of Mina al-Bakr around the middle of August in anticipation of resumed Iraqi exports.
A U.S. trader said the talked price for prospective Bayoil cargoes was at Dated Brent -$2.00 for delivery to the U.S. Gulf in late August to early September.

Well-placed U.N. sources told Reuters earlier Thursday that the aid distribution plan necessary for clinching the oil-for-food deal's resumption was only days away from gaining approval. Once the aid plan is cemented, Iraq can trigger the deal's start after submitting a pricing formula for selling new oil contracts.
